title: Where Assessment Validation and Responsible AI Meet

bias_targets.methodology: The paper does not empirically measure specific demographic biases in a new experiment, but rather proposes a theoretical framework for evaluating and mitigating bias in AI-powered educational assessments. The methodology relies on integrating Responsible AI (RAI) principles, utilizing human-in-the-loop review processes, and applying quantitative analyses such as Differential Item Functioning (DIF) to ensure test items function comparably across different test-taker subgroup populations.

Evaluated conceptually through a literature review of automated scoring systems. The paper references seven theoretical categories of bias (historical, representation, measurement, aggregation, learning/algorithmic, evaluation, and deployment bias) and proposes mitigating them via alignment with assessment validation theory, construct-relevant rubrics, and independent human-system agreement evaluations.
